instruction:
Use PostgreSQL's current Backup and Restore chapter, SQLite's https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html and linked VACUUM documentation, and DuckDB 2.0's https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/statements/export and CHECKPOINT reference. Record the documentation versions shown. Compare six approaches: PostgreSQL SQL dump; PostgreSQL base backup with continuous WAL archiving; SQLite Online Backup API; SQLite VACUUM INTO; DuckDB EXPORT DATABASE; and DuckDB CHECKPOINT. State each operation's purpose, output and scope, documented consistency/concurrency conditions, and whether it produces a separately restorable export or instead updates an active database file. Resolve six requirements: moving a PostgreSQL database to a newer major version; recovering PostgreSQL to just before an unwanted change; backing up a live SQLite database in increments; making a compact SQLite copy without deleted-content remnants; exporting DuckDB schema, tables, views and sequences for later import; and checkpointing DuckDB while another transaction holds relevant work. Explain ordinary versus FORCE checkpoint behavior under the version shown, and why synchronizing WAL into a database file is not by itself a separate backup copy. Cite controlling sections, include documented trigger omissions and fresh-target import restrictions, keep restore scope explicit, and separate backup content from logs needed for point-in-time recovery. Read documentation only; do not execute SQL, programs or backups.

Stopping condition: Stop when six operation comparisons and six cited requirement assessments explain output, consistency, concurrency and recovery scope without executing any example.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Agent must record the documentation versions shown for PostgreSQL, SQLite, and DuckDB 2.0. Full credit if all three versions are identified from the respective pages, OR if the agent attempts to access the pages and clearly reports that a site is inaccessible or the version is not listed. Partial credit if some accessible versions are missed.

Agent must compare PostgreSQL SQL dump, PostgreSQL base backup with continuous WAL, SQLite Online Backup API, SQLite VACUUM INTO, DuckDB EXPORT DATABASE, and DuckDB CHECKPOINT. For each, state purpose, output, scope, documented consistency/concurrency conditions, and whether it produces a separately restorable export or updates an active file. Full credit for all six fully analyzed based on available docs, OR if the agent correctly notes which docs were inaccessible. Partial credit for missing approaches or missing details on accessible docs.

items.criterion: Resolve Six Backup and Recovery Requirements
items.description: Agent must resolve: 1) Moving PostgreSQL to a newer major version; 2) Recovering PostgreSQL to before an unwanted change (PITR); 3) Backing up a live SQLite database in increments; 4) Making a compact SQLite copy without remnants; 5) Exporting DuckDB schema, tables, views, sequences; 6) Checkpointing DuckDB with active transactions holding work. Full credit for correctly resolving all six based on the docs, OR identifying which cannot be resolved due to site inaccessibility. Partial credit for resolving fewer than six when docs are available.

items.criterion: Explain DuckDB Checkpoint Behavior and WAL Sync Limitations
items.description: Agent must explain ordinary versus FORCE checkpoint behavior under DuckDB 2.0, and explain why synchronizing WAL into a database file is not by itself a separate backup copy. Full credit for clear explanation of both points from the docs, OR for noting if the specific DuckDB docs were inaccessible. Partial credit if only one is correctly explained when docs are available.

items.criterion: Include Specific Citations and Technical Constraints
items.description: Agent must cite controlling sections, include documented trigger omissions, fresh-target import restrictions, keep restore scope explicit, and separate backup content from logs needed for PITR. Full credit for addressing all these nuances correctly based on the documentation, OR reporting if the documentation pages were unreachable. Partial credit for missing citations or constraints that were available. Identify trigger omissions only where documented for the relevant operation/version. Include the controlling documentation source URLs.
